tempo_convention: typical_bpm_range is the notated / DAW-project tempo: the full-time quarter-note BPM a producer sets the session to and DJ metadata quotes (trap, drill, dubstep, chillstep ~140, not their ~70 half-time feel; drum-and-bass ~174, not 87). Genuinely slow or fast genres (drone, doom, speedcore) keep their literal tempo. Detected BPM is always matched octave-folded (x1/2, x1, x2) because beat trackers lock to half or double this pulse.
note: SP-07 + 2026-07-09 underground expansion + 2026-07-10 reference enrichment (spec §8): 185 genres. Clustered by parent family (alphabetical) with the base genre first in each cluster followed by alphabetical variants; the 2026-07-10 additions (country, corridos-tumbados, funk, trap-soul, cinematic, rock, pop-punk, blues, reggae, dancehall) are appended at the end. 2026-07-15: added explicit stem_energy_balance blocks to a representative genre subset (trap, pop, rock, house, jazz, acoustic). 2026-07-24: appended 15 pop-adjacent and 15 hip-hop-adjacent subgenres at the tail of the pop and hip-hop family clusters; inserted 8 rock-adjacent (after stoner-rock) and 8 R&B-adjacent (after soul) subgenres within their family clusters. 2026-11-16 (MEAS-1): spectral_centroid_hz, low_end_weight, spectral_tilt_target_db_per_octave, crest_factor_target_db and stereo_width_range of the 113 genres with at least 6 corpus tracks are measured (genre_corpus_stats.json; each such entry has a 'measured' block); loudness, LRA and the song-level norms stay hand-set.
